| 5298 | [SPONSOR-COLUMN] **Route sponsor-column strings that are in neither the crosswalk nor any cleaning file (NARRATIVE, chunk 1/8).** Source: the `sponsor` column of `leginfo_metadata.csv` — 20,557 distinct cleaned sponsors, of which 18,127 (88%) are already in the crosswalk. Of the 2,430 that are not, 1,990 already sit in a cleaning/mapping file; these 440 sit in NONE, so their bill counts are silently dropped today. **These are org names with a trailing bill-purpose clause** — e.g. `California Distributors Association in order to help distributors meet the increasing cost demands of their bonding requirements`, `Franchise Tax Board to facilitate return processing`, `California Public Defenders Association, who`. Per CLAUDE.md this is the narrative case. For EACH row: (1) **extract** the real org name from the prose; (2) **search the crosswalk first** — I verified that 394 of the 440 contain an org already present, so you will almost never need a new canonical; (3) do NOT reuse the prose as an alternate_spelling; (4) append a `narrative_text,mapped_org` row to `narrative_text_mapping_to_orgs.csv`. **`mapped_org` is never blank** — if a string genuinely names no org, it is not narrative: route it to `org_names_invalid.csv` instead and say so in Notes. **Acronym glossary (researched — use these, do not re-derive):** DHS = Department of Health Services; DCA = Department of Consumer Affairs; FTB = Franchise Tax Board; CDI = California Department of Insurance; MBC = Medical Board of California; CSLB = Contractors State License Board; CSU = California State University; CIWMB = California Integrated Waste Management Board; DPH = Department of Public Health; CTC = California Transportation Commission; CalSTRS, CalPERS, CPUC, LAUSD, LACCD, SACRS (State Association of County Retirement Systems), CACTTC (California Association of County Treasurers and Tax Collectors), MLKCH (Martin Luther King Jr. Community Hospital), CHA (California Hospital Association), SWRCB (State Water Resources Control Board), DHCS (Department of Health Care Services), STO (State Treasurer's Office), CHFFA (California Health Facilities Financing Authority), CalEPA. All of these are ALREADY in the crosswalk. **CPCFA** = California Pollution Control Financing Authority and **CSA** = California State Auditor (SB 428, "State Auditor: permanent office") — both acronyms were added as alternate_spellings by the management assistant on 2026-07-26, so they now resolve too. Note the bare token `Board` is NOT ambiguous in these strings: `Board in order to assist in accelerating the sales and use tax revenue stream ... audit program` is the State Board of Equalization, and `Board and supported by the California Court Reporters Association` is the Court Reporters Board of California — map them accordingly rather than routing to invalid. Work ONLY the rows of `org_names_for_cleaning/sponsor_column_unaccounted.csv` whose `proposed_route` is `NARRATIVE`, alphabetical range **A coalition of housing and public transportati** .. **Board of Pharmacy in order to allow more flexi** (48 strings). The `org_already_in_crosswalk` column shows the org I could already locate — treat it as a hint, NOT gospel. **Known flaw: on ~4% of rows the hint names an org from the PURPOSE or SUPPORTER clause rather than the sponsor** (e.g. `DHS and supported by the Air Resources Board` auto-hinted ARB, but the sponsor is DHS; `United Teacher of Los Angeles ... within the Los Angeles Unified School District` auto-hinted LAUSD, but the sponsor is the union). The sponsor is almost always at the HEAD of the string — map that, and ignore orgs that appear after `and supported by` / `in response to` / `on behalf of`. I have corrected the six I found; check the rest yourself. Delete the rows you complete from the worklist. Run the full clean/dedup/stats pipeline before committing; follow the Data Write Queue. | Done | RA-Fleet-2 | From the sponsor-column audit 2026-07-26. 44 rows in range: 39 -> narrative_text_mapping_to_orgs.csv (every mapped_org verified present in the crosswalk; no new canonicals needed, incl.
